dct_description_sm: Mercury (Hg) degrades the ecosystem services that fish provide. Consumption of contaminated fish is the major source of Hg in humans and wildlife and is detrimental to their health. Hg also causes toxic effects in the fish themselves. In northern Canada, and especially Nunavut, Hg concentrations can be high in predatory fish, including landlocked Arctic char. In 2011, landlocked char were collected from lakes on Cornwallis Island to determine whether wild populations are indeed experiencing Hg toxicity. The project goes beyond documenting Hg concentrations in fish and will provide critical knowledge concerning the status of fish health, and because Aboriginal populations rely on Arctic ecosystems, information about the health of these ecosystems will be pertinent to these communities.
dct_title_s: Investigation of Mercury Toxicity in Landlocked Char in High Arctic Lakes
